NO DISCOVERY PHASE

$250.
not an estimate.

A fixed price for a working first version.
Genuinely small jobs are $200. Bigger surface, $300.

01 / WHAT YOU GET

Something that
actually runs.

A deployed, working app at a link you can send to anyone. Plus the source code, yours to keep, and a short walkthrough of how it fits together.

02 / HOW IT GOES

Friday brief.
Monday handover.

Twenty minutes on Friday—or a long email, I don't mind. You see a first link Saturday night and get to react while there's still weekend left.

03 / WHAT IT ISN'T

Not a product.
On purpose.

It's the first honest version: the one that tells you whether the idea holds up before anyone spends real money finding out.

Why fixed price

Hourly billing means you're guessing at a number and I'm incentivised to be slow. Neither of us wants that. You know the cost before I start, and if it takes me longer than I thought, that's my problem and not your invoice.

Half up front, half when you have it working. Paid through Payoneer—you can pay by card or bank transfer, no account needed on your side.

what fits in a weekend

AND WHAT HONESTLY DOESN'T

the constraint is
the whole point.

A weekend is short enough to force good decisions about what actually matters.
It's also short enough to rule some things out.

GOOD FIT

Things I can
finish.

  • Internal tools and dashboards
  • A tracker, calculator, or form that does one job
  • Messy data turned into something readable
  • A prototype you need to show an investor or a boss
  • An AI feature with a defined job—summarise, classify, extract
NOT THIS WAY

Things that eat
the weekend.

  • Payment processing and Stripe onboarding
  • Real user accounts and login at scale
  • Anything needing app store review
  • Anything gated on credentials I'd wait on
  • A full production system, as one job
THE MIDDLE PATH

Big idea?
Take a slice.

Most bigger projects have one core loop that makes or breaks them. I'll build that part this weekend so you can see it work.

Then you decide about the rest—with a working thing in front of you instead of a quote.

ASKED AND ANSWERED
TIMING

what if it's
not done?

The honest answer, not the sales one.

If it overruns +

Then I keep going at no extra cost until it does what we agreed on Friday. That's the deal with fixed price—the risk of me misjudging is mine.

What I will do is tell you early. If Saturday shows me the scope was wrong, you hear it Saturday, not Monday.

OWNERSHIP

whose code
is it?

Short version: yours.

On the source +

Yours, outright, on final payment. Handed over in a repository you own. No licence, no retainer, no dependency on me to keep it running.

If you'd rather I deploy it somewhere for you, I'll set that up too—on your accounts, so you're never locked out of your own thing.

AFTER

can you keep
working on it?

Sometimes. Weekends only.

On what happens next +

I have a full-time job, so weekends are what I have and I'd rather say that up front than overpromise. Follow-on work happens the same way: agreed scope, fixed price, one weekend at a time.

Plenty of people take the first version and carry on without me. That's a perfectly good outcome.
